questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Nullity of a Matrix Using Row Reduction
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(A)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 7 \\ 6 & -3 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 13 \\ 6 & -3 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(A)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))=0.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Dimension of the Null Space of Matrices Using Inspection
questions.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Find $\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C)).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=1.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has $2$ pivot columns and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $4$th columns). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=2.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has $4$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=0.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C))=1+2+0=3.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix Given the Number of Non-Pivot Columns
questions.problem: Let $Q$ be a $5\times 8$ matrix that has $5$ pivot columns. What is the dimension of the null space of $Q?$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $\text{dim(Null}(Q))$ is the number of non-pivot columns in $Q.$ 

Since $Q$ has $8$ columns and $5$ of them are pivots, then the number of non-pivot columns in $Q$ is 

$$
8-5=3.
$$

Therefore, $\text{dim(Null}(Q))=3.$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Find $\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C)).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 8 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $3$rd columns). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd  column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C))=2+1+1=4.
$$
